searchText: In the BeaconState debug endpoint for Altair, are we encoding the participation-registry bit-flags list as one big hex string (since each validator is a byte), or as a list of N numbers (not strings)? I think the hex-string makes more sense Implementing it as hex-string in my tooling for now, It's easy to get a specific byte still, more efficient, and more similar to bitlists/bitvectors than a list of integers really. We have it as a list of integers currently, but can change to a hex-encoded string easily enough. I mostly use the JSON debug endpoints for manual mucking around, and munging with `jq`, etc, and would prefer a list for these purposes. I think any "more serious" tooling should use the SSZ endpoint <@!602753420033785856> good point about `jq`. Still feels inefficient to change every byte to an int though. The BeaconState debug endpoint as a whole is too heavy for most serious applications. However, the participation-flags are super useful for performance-tracking / explorers still. Maybe we should even have an endpoint that just returns that. if we're creating a separate endpoint for it, it would be nice if the encoding is the same And I know <@!514429265001971732> is waiting for the Altair participation-flag registry. It makes attestation performance tracking easy For the separate endpoint it might be nice to have optional validator IDs? Like: _give me the participation bits for validators x, y, z_ Although explorers will likely want bits for all validators At 400K validators, the response is still under 1 MB, pretty good to track large amounts of participation data So don't think we need pagination, especially since it's likely just a copy from the head state anyway Filtering is nice for small users though, hmm Maybe the bulk endpoint is sufficient for now, and we can add a separate filtering option later Another interesting thing is that we use only 3 bits per byte really so in hex encoding, half of the output nibbles are `0` And with the integer option we get `,` instead Hmm, Go by default json-encodes a `[]uint8` as base64, so it has to explicitly implement one or the other option. Encoding to hex at least gives you fixed output length, whereas `[]int` does not (if we have more than 4 bits per byte). Idk, probably overthinking it So Teku implements it as a `MutableList<SSZByte>`, Nimbus as a `HashList[ParticipationFlags, Limit VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_LIMIT]`, and Prysm as a `[]byte` (protobuf `bytes` really). <@!311971895828283393> would prysm be able to encode it (the participation flags in Altair BeaconState) as json-list of numbers? Or we can change the other clients to hex-encoding of the list. As long as we can agree on something Given that it is a list of `uint8` it seems like the canonical representation should indeed be a list of numbers. this is what nimbus will encode it as, if we do "nothing" anectdotally and separately, we have a tool that extracts similar bits for mainnet up to now (for performance tracking) - an sqlite database that collects all _misses_ of any form (anything that is not a perfect attestation) right now lands at 5.5gb for all validators and epochs of mainnet I think this is something we could do with type aliases, and now we have strong typing for the specific-eth2 types. We also have a custom way of transcoding these types into JSON responses for the API in any way we want, so we should be OK I believe. Thanks for letting us know early! Ok, then we'll encode the current and previous epoch participation fields of the BeaconState as a list of numbers, and not a hex-encoded byte string. ok so basically this would be reflected in the rest api as a change to `BeaconStateAltair` so that participation is a list of numbers, rather than the current bytes definition...

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: In the BeaconState debug endpoint for Altair, are we encoding the participation-registry bit-flags list as one big hex string (since each validator is a byte), or as a list of N numbers (not strings)? I think the hex-string makes more sense

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Implementing it as hex-string in my tooling for now, It's easy to get a specific byte still, more efficient, and more similar to bitlists/bitvectors than a list of integers really.

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
We have it as a list of integers currently, but can change to a hex-encoded string easily enough.

I mostly use the JSON debug endpoints for manual mucking around, and munging with `jq`, etc, and would prefer a list for these purposes. I think any "more serious" tooling should use the SSZ endpoint

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: <@!602753420033785856> good point about `jq`. Still feels inefficient to change every byte to an int though. The BeaconState debug endpoint as a whole is too heavy for most serious applications. However, the participation-flags are super useful for performance-tracking / explorers still. Maybe we should even have an endpoint that just returns that.

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: if we're creating a separate endpoint for it, it would be nice if the encoding is the same

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: And I know <@!514429265001971732> is waiting for the Altair participation-flag registry. It makes attestation performance tracking easy

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: For the separate endpoint it might be nice to have optional validator IDs? Like: _give me the participation bits for validators x, y, z_

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: Although explorers will likely want bits for all validators

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: At 400K validators, the response is still under 1 MB, pretty good to track large amounts of participation data

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: So don't think we need pagination, especially since it's likely just a copy from the head state anyway

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Filtering is nice for small users though, hmm

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: Maybe the bulk endpoint is sufficient for now, and we can add a separate filtering option later

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Another interesting thing is that we use only 3 bits per byte really

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: so in hex encoding, half of the output nibbles are `0`

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: And with the integer option we get `,` instead

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Hmm, Go by default json-encodes a `[]uint8` as base64, so it has to explicitly implement  one or the other option. Encoding to hex at least gives you fixed output length, whereas `[]int` does not (if we have more than 4 bits per byte).

excerpts.author: protolambda

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: So Teku implements it as a `MutableList<SSZByte>`, Nimbus as a `HashList[ParticipationFlags, Limit VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_LIMIT]`, and Prysm as a `[]byte` (protobuf `bytes` really). <@!311971895828283393> would prysm be able to encode it (the participation flags in Altair BeaconState) as json-list of numbers?

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Or we can change the other clients to hex-encoding of the list. As long as we can agree on something

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Given that it is a list of `uint8` it seems like the canonical representation should indeed be a list of numbers.

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: this is what nimbus will encode it as, if we do "nothing"

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: anectdotally and separately, we have a tool that extracts similar bits for mainnet up to now (for performance tracking) - an sqlite database that collects all _misses_ of any form (anything that is not a perfect attestation) right now lands at 5.5gb for all validators and epochs of mainnet

excerpts.author: raulj
excerpts.content: I think this is something we could do with type aliases, and now we have strong typing for the specific-eth2 types. We also have a custom way of transcoding these types into JSON responses for the API in any way we want, so we should be OK I believe. Thanks for letting us know early!

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Ok, then we'll encode the current and previous epoch participation fields of the BeaconState as a list of numbers, and not a hex-encoded byte string.

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: ok so basically this would be reflected in the rest api as a change to `BeaconStateAltair` so that participation is a list of numbers, rather than the current bytes definition...
